And on this account, many of the citizens of Melitene perished.
And in the year 536
(530 of the Arabs),
Khwarazm Shah sent to the king of the inner Huns (men) who had not converted to Islam,
who are called by the Arabs 'Kafir Turk',
and he invited and summoned him to battle against Sultan Sanjar,
because Sanjar had killed the brother of Khwarazm Shah.
And when those Huns had prepared themselves with three hundred thousand,
Sanjar gathered one hundred thousand,
and he crossed the River Gihon (Oxus).
And he encountered the Huns,
and the men on his side were utterly broken.
It is said
that with six persons he escaped, and came and entered the city of Balkh.
And his wife and his granddaughter were captured,
and four thousand other women.
And of those one hundred thousand, not one was saved from the sword or captivity.
And in the year 1454
of the Greeks,
Malik Mahmud died in Caesarea.
And he commanded
that Dhu al-Nun, his son, should reign in his place.
His wife, however, brought Yaqub Arslan his brother,
and she became his wife,
and he reigned in Sebastia.
And Dhu al-Nun fled to Simandu,
and he gained control over Caesarea.
And Dawlah, another brother, came,
and Yunus, lord of the fortress of Masara, agreed with him.
And they came against Melitene,
but they were unable to take it,
and they abandoned it, went, and encamped against Arqa.
Then the Khatun,
she who was married to Yaqub Arslan,
sent two thousand men to come to Melitene and guard it,
and to bring out the Turks who were in it and send them to Sebastia.
Then the Turks inside were enraged,
and with axes they broke open the city gate called that of Buridya,
because the governor was not permitting them to leave,
and they came out and put to flight those two thousand.
And on that very day, they sent and brought Dawlah,
and made him ruler over Melitene.
Then Sultan Mas'ud of Iconium came against Sebastia,
and plundered it and devastated it.
And he also came against Melitene and encamped against it on the seventeenth of Nisan,
and set up catapults,
and pressed it hard with war.
And Dawlah also, from within, inflicted evils on the Christian chiefs with exactions, taking and giving to the warriors.
